extracted.intended_audience: Korean Patent Office examiners and patent applicants (handling foreign-language applications, divisional/converted applications, and translations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and procedural handling of foreign‑language patent applications, corrections of Korean translations, divisional/converted applications, domestic priority claims, and related issues under the Korean Patent Act. Covers when Korean translations may be relied on, how mistranslation corrections are evaluated, and substantive/time/filing requirements for division and conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of introduction of new matter beyond the Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there were no errors in the Korean translations but the Korean translations have become different from the foreign language specification due to unnecessary and irrelevant correction, a rejection shall be issued on the ground of introduction of new matter beyond the Korean translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sequence: (1) foreign language application as filed (A), (2) specification deemed amended after submission of Korean translation (A->A), (3) Korean translations are corrected (A->B), (4) specification is un-amended. If the corrected Korean translation (B) differs from the foreign-language specification and introduces matter beyond the Korean translation, issue rejection for new matter beyond the Korean translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of introduction of new matter beyond the foreign language specification and the Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification for examination is amended beyond the scope of corrected Korean translations and the foreign language specification, a rejection shall be issued on the ground of introduction of new matter beyond the foreign language specification and the Korean translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (1) foreign language specification as filed (A), (2) specification deemed amended after submission of Korean translations (A->B), (3) Korean translations corrected (B->C), (4) specification is amended (B->D). If the specification for examination (D) is beyond the corrected Korean translations (C) and the foreign language specification (A), it constitutes new matter. Applicant must correct wrong correction of mistranslation (C->A) and amend the specification for examination accordingly (D->A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in evaluating correction of a mistranslation — appropriateness not a rejection ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a mistranslation is corrected, appropriateness and inappropriateness thereof shall not constitute reasons for rejection or reasons for amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction of a mistranslation per se should not be rejected merely because its correctness is debatable; examiners should not treat appropriateness as a ground for rejection or forced amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in evaluating correction of a mistranslation — insufficient reasons and amendment/invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentary materials accompanied by a statement of correction of a mistranslation do not explain reasons for correction or where reasons for correction are not sufficiently described so that appropriateness is hard to evaluate, amendment shall be ordered on the ground of insufficient reasons for correction; if amendment cannot relieve insufficient reasons, correction of mistranslations itself shall be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's materials do not objectively explain why the pre-amendment translation is unreasonable and post-amendment translation is reasonable (Example 1), or if reasons (e.g., interpretation of context or common general knowledge) are not sufficiently described (Example 2), order amendment for clarification. If defects cannot be cured, invalidate the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to rely on Korean translations for prior art searching
rubrics_metrics.description: When a foreign language specification and its Korean translations are generally identical, it is sufficient to search only the Korean translations for prior art purposes such as novelty and enlarged concept of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if it is doubtful that the Korean translations differ from the foreign language specification, the scope of search shall be expanded to include the specification of the foreign language patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review for foreign-language prior art in enlarged concept of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign language patent application serves as prior art for the enlarged concept of novelty, the foreign language specification should finally be reviewed even though the search may be based on the Korean specification (laid open to public inspection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final determination of prior art effect must be made on the foreign language specification; initial searching may rely on Korean translations but confirm with the original when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of notice of grounds for rejection when citing foreign-language prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign language patent application is cited as 'prior art for enlarged concept of novelty', a notice of grounds for rejection shall be stated so that the foreign language specification corresponding to the Korean specification constitute reasons for rejection, with reference to the Korean specification (which are amended based on Korean translations) already laid open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should make clear that the foreign-language text underlies the rejection and cite the corresponding Korean specification that is publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner response to applicant's arguments regarding foreign-language prior art disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant argues that the invention under examination is not disclosed in the foreign language specification relied upon as prior art, the examiner's reasons for rejection shall be overcome if the applicant successfully demonstrates lack of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is found in a pending foreign language application, the examiner shall issue a notice of grounds for rejection on the ground of introduction of new matter to that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of first-to-file rule when prior-filed application contains new matter beyond foreign-language specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention claimed in a prior-filed application includes new matter beyond the foreign language specification, the claimed invention cannot be relied on in issuing a rejection under Article 36(1)-(3) of the Patent Act. New matter introduced in a prior-filed application claim cannot be a bar to a later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same rule applies to foreign language applications to conform to the first-to-file principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic concept: treating foreign-language applications as regular domestic applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign language application is considered a regular domestic application; divisional, converted, or applications with domestic priority claims shall be permitted accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing-date effects for division/conversion/priority are normally evaluated on the basis of the foreign language specification, not Korean translations; however, because foreign-language specifications often coincide with Korean translations, the examiner may depend on Korean translations in determining retroactive filing date when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining scope for divisional applications from a foreign-language parent
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive requirement for a divisional application — that it be within the scope of matters described in the specification or drawings originally attached to the parent application — is based on the disclosure of the foreign language specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a foreign-language specification likely coincides with Korean translations, in practice the examiner shall compare the Korean translations of the parent with the specification of the divisional during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination practice when divisional application itself is a foreign-language application
rubrics_metrics.description: When a divisional application is filed in a foreign language, a specification deemed amended according to the Korean translations (rather than the foreign language specification) shall be compared with the specification of the parent application to determine whether substantive requirements are satisfied; proscription of new matter is separately evaluated by comparing the foreign language specification of the divisional application and the amended specification for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defects in the divisional specification are rectified through amendment based on Korean translations and subsequent amendment, the divisional shall be deemed legitimate even if the original divisional specification did not satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing a divisional application relative to Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the parent application of a divisional application is a foreign language application, a divisional application cannot be permitted before the submission of the Korean translations of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although divisional applications are permitted within the same time frames as regular applications, the prerequisite is submission of Korean translations of the parent when the parent was filed in a foreign language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and timing for converted applications based on foreign-language originals
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application must fall within the scope of matters described in the specification of the original application; where Korean translations have been submitted they shall be compared with the specification and drawings of the converted application. A converted application cannot be filed before submission of the Korean translations of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a converted application itself is a foreign language application, compare the specification amended based on Korean translations (not the foreign-language spec) with the original application's specification to determine substantive requirements; proscription of new matter is separately evaluated by comparing specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating domestic priority claims when prior-filed application is foreign-language
rubrics_metrics.description: If Korean translations of a prior-filed foreign-language application have been filed, effects of a domestic priority claim shall be evaluated by comparing the Korean translations of the prior-filed application and the specification and drawings of the application claiming domestic priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Korean translations of the prior-filed application are not yet filed at the time the domestic-priority‑claiming application is filed, compare the original specification and drawings of the prior-filed application with those of the application claiming domestic priority. In other cases, compare the prior-filed spec/drawings and the foreign-language application claiming domestic priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of international patent applications filed in a foreign language
rubrics_metrics.description: International patent applications filed in a foreign language shall be handled identically to foreign-language patent applications. International applications may correct mistranslations based on specification and drawings filed on the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An international patent application filed in a foreign language can be invalidated or rejected on the ground of introduction of new matter in an original text; the determination shall be based on the specification submitted up to the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 52 — divisional application filing prerequisites and foreign-language caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has filed a patent application for two or more inventions may divide a portion into one or more applications within the scope of disclosure of the original specification or drawings during specified periods. If the patent application has been filed in a foreign language, it may be divided only when the Korean translation pursuant to Article 42-3(2) has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted periods include (1) the period during which amendments can be made under Article 47(1); (2) within 30 days from service of a certified copy of decision to reject (with extensions); (3) within three months from service of certified copy of decision to grant or certain trial decisions, subject to specific provisos. Also, special rules allow submission of Korean translation for divisional filed in foreign language within 30 days from divisional filing date (with exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons who may file a divisional application and identity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who may file a divisional application is the applicant who filed the parent application or his/her successor; where an application is jointly filed, applicants of the divisional shall be identical to those who filed the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recognize identity between parent and divisional applicants, the following shall be met: (i) same domicile or business address of the applicants, (ii) same name or title of the applicants, and (iii) same seal of the applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time requirement and pendency for filing divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The time of filing a divisional application is categorized by filing date and other procedural events; critically, the parent application must be pending before KIPO at the time of filing a divisional application — if the parent has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or the decision to reject has become final and binding, a divisional cannot be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a divisional is filed on the day the parent proceeding is terminated (withdrawn/abandoned), the divisional shall be treated as filed when the parent was pending, because it is difficult to distinguish which proceeding occurred first. Detailed period rules depend on filing date eras and statutory events (examination requests, notices, appeals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive requirement for divisional applications — disclosure scope and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention eligible for a divisional application is an invention within the scope of subject matter disclosed in the original specification or drawings of the parent application. All inventions in the divisional must be disclosed in the parent; if any single invention in the divisional is not contained in the parent, the divisional is invalid or has grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners shall determine whether the invention is explicitly described or is obviously recognized as implicitly described. The specification/drawings originally attached to the parent form the basis of validity: invent ions deleted later from the parent but originally disclosed remain eligible for division; inventions newly added to the parent by amendment are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure of filing a divisional application — formality and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be filed by attaching the specification and necessary documents to a written patent application in the prescribed Form; the divisional must state its purport and indicate the parent patent application which forms the basis of division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parent application is not indicated, the divisional will not be recognized as legitimate. Amendments changing the indicated parent after filing are not accepted except for obvious errors. Applicants normally should amend the parent to differentiate claims, but if divisional inventions are disclosed only in description or drawings, amending the parent is not required. Claims for disclosure exceptions or priority must be stated and evidential documents submitted within prescribed periods (e.g., 30 days for disclosure exception, three months for priority). Applicants may rely on evidential documents already submitted for the parent if they state the purport of using the parent documents; otherwise the examiner will request amendment for missing formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of a divisional application — retention of parent's filing date and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application generally retains the same filing date as the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where the divisional shall be deemed filed when actually filed include cases where the divisional corresponds to 'another application' under Article 29(3) (e.g., converted forms where new subject matter added) or other unfair situations; in such cases the divisional cannot enjoy the parent's filing date for the newly added subject matter.
